Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, CTO; Jordan Lee, Chief Revenue Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Product Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Marketing Officer; and Rachel Kim, Chief Customer Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on eight key areas: ARR growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, CAC trends, free cash flow generation, NRR performance, Rule of 40 achievement, churn analysis and mitigation, sales efficiency including cycle lengths and conversions, and expansion revenue from existing customers.

These metrics highlight the strength of our land-and-expand model and AI-infused DevOps platform. We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $528 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $169 million.

Turning first to our core top-line metric: Annual Recurring Revenue, or ARR. As of the end of Q3 FY2024, our total ARR reached $1.28 billion, up an impressive 28% year-over-year from $1.0 billion in Q3 FY2023, and 7% quarter-over-quarter from $1.2 billion at the end of Q2. This marks our 12th straight quarter of at least 25% YoY ARR growth, underscoring the durability of our land-and-expand model even as many SaaS peers in spaces like Salesforce or ServiceNow deal with longer sales cycles and weaker SMB demand.

Net new ARR this quarter totaled $80 million. New logo ARR contributed $32 million, or 40%, driven by enterprise wins. We secured 15 deals over $1 million in ACV, including a landmark $5 million multi-year contract with a Fortune 50 financial services firm adopting our CloudForge Platform for their full DevOps stack—end-to-end CI/CD pipelines integrated with Kubernetes and GitOps workflows. This shows our traction in regulated verticals, where compliance like SOC 2 Type II and FedRAMP sets us apart from GitLab and Harness.

Expansion ARR was the standout at $42 million, or 52.5%, with dollar-based NRR at 118%. Upsells stemmed from deeper usage of AI-native features like the AutoScale Optimizer launched in Q1, which dynamically rightsizes compute resources and delivers 30-40% cost savings. This shone in media and gaming customers, similar to Unity or Electronic Arts deployments.

Churn and contraction were minimal at -$4 million, with gross dollar retention at 98% and NRR at 118%. Our customer success teams keep voluntary churn low despite some mid-market pricing pushback.

By region, North America is 72% of ARR at $922 million, up 30% YoY, boosted by AWS and Azure partnerships. EMEA grew 35% to $218 million (17%), strong in DACH and UK finance hubs with GDPR data sovereignty. APAC, 11% at $140 million, grew 42%, highlighted by a hyperscale Japan telco win with edge computing for low-latency CI/CD.

These results affirm our AI-infused DevOps shift, with generative AI for predictive failure detection and automated remediation taking share from Jenkins or Bamboo. Q2's ForgeAI Agents release drove 25% higher platform velocity, leading to seat expansions and multi-product use. For Q4, we expect $85-95 million net new ARR, implying FY2024 ARR around $1.35 billion, or 32% YoY at midpoint, with NRR to 120%.

This is high-quality growth, with Rule of 40 at 68 on a cash flow basis.

Next, on customer acquisition cost, or CAC trends, which show efficiency gains in our go-to-market. CAC is total sales and marketing expenses divided by new customers, on a net new ARR basis. In Q3 FY2024, blended CAC was $428 per new customer, down 12% sequentially from $487 and 28% YoY from $595. This is our sixth straight quarter of reduction, beating our sub-$450 year-end target and Bessemer's $520 median for peers.

By segment, SMB CAC fell to $285, down 15% QoQ via PLG, with 1.8x usage expansion like Notion or Atlassian. Enterprise CAC at $1,250 improved 22% YoY as sales cycles shortened to 78 days from 95, for AI workflow automation like Salesforce Einstein.

Performance marketing led: Google Ads and LinkedIn CPCs at $4.20, 4.2x ROAS via ML optimization. Content and SEO (35% leads) pay back in 9 months, aided by hybrid work content. Partnerships like AWS Marketplace and Microsoft AppSource drove 22% new logos, cutting CAC 40%, Snowflake-style.

North America (68% new ARR) CAC $410, EMEA $465 but improving to $420 with inbound, APAC $380 down 32% via Tencent Cloud and Sakura edition for 2.5x LTV.

LTV:CAC at 4.8x, payback 11.2 months from 14.6. We've shifted 25% SMG budget to PLG like LeadGenix AI, boosting pipeline 42%. Q4 CAC $410-420, with GenAI upsells.

Now, free cash flow, a key non-GAAP metric. We generated $152 million in FCF, up 28% YoY from $119 million. TTM FCF $612 million, up 32%, margin 28% of revenue from 22%. On track for $650-675 million full-year, aligning with Rule of 40 discipline.

FCF is operating cash flow minus CapEx. OCF $178 million up 25% YoY, CapEx $26 million or 5% revenue.

Drivers: Revenue $528 million up 32%, recurring up 35% to $2.1 billion ARR equivalent, DBNRR 118%. Collections 105% billings, DSOs to 47 from 52 via Stripe/Zuora.

Operating leverage: non-GAAP op margins 32% up 450 bps, gross 82% from multi-tenant AWS/Azure. CAC payback 16 months from 19, R&D $110 million (21%) on GenAI co-pilot at 15% attach.

Working capital: deferred revenue $1.4 billion up 28%, $25 million R&D tax refund.

Regions: NA $104 million (68%) up 35%, EMEA $32 million up 45% from Paris DC, APAC $16 million up 12%.

Headwinds managed: headcount to 2,800, $18 million SBC, CapEx up for GPUs offset by AWS savings.

YTD $200 million buybacks at $85/share, $400 million left. Eyeing cyber tuck-ins like CrowdStrike modules.

Q4 FCF $160-170 million, margins 29%, Adobe-style scale.

On NRR performance, a land-and-expand cornerstone. Q3 NRR 115%, 11th quarter above 110%, up 300 bps YoY from 112%. Stickiness from AI collaboration platform in hybrid work and GenAI, like Slack/Notion post-ChatGPT.

Expansion added 28 points, net 25% from Enterprise upsells—18% adopted ForgeAI agents for devops/sales automation like Einstein. Usage pricing $12 million incremental ARR up 40% QoQ. Cross-sell Security Analytics 32% attach. NA 30%, EMEA 22% with GDPR AI.

Contraction 6 points flat QoQ, SMB from budget downsizes mitigated by Retention Shield predictive analytics. Enterprise <2%.

Churn 4% down 100 bps YoY, Enterprise logo 1.2% from switching costs, SMB 7% from pricing sunset. 2022 cohorts 92% at 24 months, beating Bessemer.

Doubling on ForgeAI 2.0 multi-modal LLMs Q4, APAC localization, dynamic pricing +5 points expansion. Q4 NRR 116-118%, $150 million pipeline.

Rule of 40: revenue growth + non-GAAP EBITDA margin. Q3 score 47%, up from 42% Q2, 38% YoY. Sixth quarter above 40%.

Revenue 35% YoY to $128 million quarterly equivalent, $22 million net new ARR, 28% expansion from AI workflows. Beats Snowflake/Datadog 25-30%, via healthcare Epic, manufacturing IoT.

EBITDA margin 12% up 300 bps, gross 82% cloud shift 65%, S&M 42% flat, NDR 118%, R&D 22% on ForgeAI reducing churn to 4.2%.

Regions: NA 68% ARR 38% YoY FedRAMP, EMEA 22%, APAC 55% SAP integrations.

PLG freemium 20% pipeline, FCF margin 8%, $450 million cash for M&A like predictive startup. Q4 48-50%, margins +100-200 bps.

Churn analysis: NRR 118% up from 115%, logo churn 4.2% annualized down 50 bps, revenue churn 2.8% below BI median 5-7%. SMB 7.5%, Enterprise 1.8%, multi-year 65% ARR.

Voluntary 65% down from 72%, involuntary 15% macro, other 20% pilots.

Voluntary: competition 35% to Looker/Power BI or Sigma; cost 25% inflation/layoffs esp EMEA 6.1%; onboarding 20% ERP hurdles CSAT<8; usage 15% low DAU/MAU, APAC UI; other 5% M&A.

Regions: NA 3.5% 120% NRR, EMEA GDPR/Brexit, APAC 5.3% China slowdown.

Mitigations $25M FY23: ChurnGuard ML 92% precision 50 signals, retained $4.2M 8x ROI, graph NN.

ForgeFast onboarding 18 days, CSMs 85% coverage QBRs 30% upsell, CSAT 9.1 NPS 52.

Expansion Packs 40% attach Predictive Forecasting, GDPR Auto-Compliance, usage pricing -25% early churn.

Pause options 90% reactivate, ABM win-back 22% $1.8M.

Regional: EMEA Atos VARs, APAC Growth Guarantee, NA vertical POCs.

Rule 40 48%, 100 bps cut adds $15M ARR. Q4 120 bps compression, $285-290M ARR exit, Snowflake consumption resilience.

Sales efficiency: sales cycle 92 days, 23% YoY better from 120, 7% QoQ from 99, top quartile vs 110-130 median.

Mid-market 65 days down 18%, PLG Freemium 42% logos 68% day1 activation Slack/Teams.

Enterprise 145 days down 12%, ForgeAI Demo 28-day PoCs.

Regions: NA 85 days 78% bookings, EMEA 105 from 140 GDPR VARs, APAC 130 beta self-serve.

Conversion 18.2% up from 14.5% YoY, ARR/sales $1.7M >$1.5 target.

MQL-SQL 42% AI scoring Clearbit/6sense, SQL-Opportunity 68% Gong 85% adherence, Opp-Close 32% Expansion pilots 128% NRR.

Initiatives: Outreach/Clari 15% velocity, Drift chats 22%, Freemium viral 1.3 28% ARR, sales eng enablement Chorus 18% quotas.

Sub-90 days YE Snowflake syncs, Singapore expansion, Rule 40 68% $250M ARR.

Expansion revenue: $28.7 million up 42% YoY from $20.2 million, 12% QoQ, NRR 121% up 300 bps >115+ target, elite like Snowflake 128%.

Upsells 62% $17.8M Enterprise 55% YoY ForgeAI Predict 28% dollars, ACV $185K-$267K.

Cross-sells 28% $8.0M ForgeSecure/Collab 38% YoY, 15% top100 multi-modules.

Seats 10% $2.9M 18% YoY 22% growth.

Regions: NA 72% $20.6M 45% fintech/healthcare, EMEA 18% $5.2M 62% GDPR, APAC 10% $2.9M 75% localization.

Initiatives: AI 40% expansions 3x insight, CSM 1:50 AI churn -22% 7-month first expand, Snowflake/Fabric flywheels 50% data growth.

Q4 35-40% YoY $120M pipeline, 68% ARR from existing up from 62%.

We continue to invest in R&D for innovation. Cash position $450 million strong for acquisitions. Updating full-year guidance: revenue $2.1 to $2.15 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for a technology update.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress advancing our AI capabilities, integrating them deeply into our core platform. Strong adoption of ForgeAI Agents is driving higher user engagement and better outcomes. We've enhanced security and scalability for enterprise demands.

Now Lisa Wong will update on the product roadmap.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Elena. We've prioritized user experience and are excited to launch AutoScale Optimizer. This feature significantly improves resource efficiency and cost savings by 30-40%. Strong adoption aligns with our strategy.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Lisa. This quarter, we boosted brand awareness and leads via digital campaigns and partnerships. We saw a 25% increase in website traffic and 40% in qualified leads, proving our initiatives' impact.

Rachel Kim:
Thank you, Tom. We're committed to exceptional experiences, improving support and onboarding. This led to a 15% increase in customer satisfaction scores.

Mike Patel:
Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, what's the competitive landscape like, and how do you plan to differentiate yourselves?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been transformative, contributing over 25% to net new ARR through expansions and new logos. Attach rates are at 28% in upsells, exceeding our 20% initial expectations by 40%. In a crowded AI DevOps space with GitLab and Harness, we differentiate via native GenAI for predictive remediation and FedRAMP compliance, securing wins like the Fortune 50 deal.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, what are your expected ROI from these investments, and what are the key challenges you anticipate?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Emily. APAC is a priority, targeting Japan telcos, India fintech, and Singapore hubs—$50B TAM per Gartner. Investments in localization like Sakura edition yield 2.5x LTV, ROI 3x in 18 months. Challenges include sales cycles and FX, but Tencent partnerships and data centers position us for 42% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, what's the impact of pricing changes on churn, and what are your long-term targets for NRR?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, David. Churn at 4.2% logo, managed via ChurnGuard ML retaining $4.2M, ForgeFast onboarding, and Expansion Packs. NRR trending 118%, up YoY. Pricing pilots reduced early churn 25%, dynamic tiers boost expansion 5 points. Long-term NRR target 120%+.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Patel with Barclays.

Anna Patel:
Can you provide more color on customer acquisition costs (CAC) and payback periods for new customers?

Mike Patel:
Sure, Anna. CAC $428 blended, down 28% YoY, SMB $285 PLG-led, Enterprise $1,250. Payback 11.2 months compressed from 14.6, LTV:CAC 4.8x via partnerships and AI prospecting.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: ARR growth (YoY and QoQ): Report actual ARR and percentage growth.
CAC trends: Report Customer Acquisition Cost and trends.
Free cash flow: Report free cash flow and explain key drivers.
NRR performance: Report NRR and explain drivers (expansion, contraction, churn).
Rule of 40: Report the Rule of 40 metric (Revenue Growth + Profit Margin).
Churn analysis: Discuss reasons for customer churn and mitigation strategies.
Sales efficiency: Discuss sales cycle length and conversion rates.
Expansion revenue: Detail revenue growth from existing customers.

aspect_summary.ARR growth (YoY and QoQ): Total ARR reached $1.28B, up 28% YoY from $1.0B and 7% QoQ from $1.2B. Net new ARR $80M, with $32M from new logos and $42M from expansion.
aspect_summary.CAC trends: Blended CAC $428 per new customer, down 12% QoQ from $487 and 28% YoY from $595. SMB CAC $285 (down 15% QoQ), Enterprise $1,250 (down 22% YoY). LTV:CAC 4.8x, payback 11.2 months from 14.6, driven by PLG, partnerships, and performance marketing.
aspect_summary.Free cash flow: Q3 FCF $152M, up 28% YoY from $119M; TTM $612M (28% margin). Drivers: OCF $178M (up 25% YoY), CapEx $26M; revenue growth 32%, DSOs to 47, op margins 32%, collections 105% billings, deferred revenue up 28%.
aspect_summary.NRR performance: Dollar-based NRR 118% (up from 115% prior, 112% YoY). Expansion $42M (28 points, from AI upsells/usage), contraction 6 points (SMB budgets), churn -$4M (4% logo churn, down YoY). Gross retention 98%.
aspect_summary.Rule of 40: 68 on cash flow basis; also 47% (revenue growth 35% + EBITDA margin 12%, up from 42% Q2). Driven by 28% ARR expansion, 82% gross margins, NRR 118%.
aspect_summary.Churn analysis: Logo churn 4.2% annualized (down 50 bps), revenue churn 2.8%; SMB 7.5%, Enterprise 1.8%. Reasons: competition 35%, cost/inflation 25%, onboarding 20%, low usage 15%. Mitigations: ChurnGuard ML (retained $4.2M, 92% precision), ForgeFast (18 days onboarding), CSMs/QBRs (CSAT 9.1, NPS 52), Expansion Packs, pause options (90% reactivate), regional strategies.
aspect_summary.Sales efficiency: Sales cycle 92 days (down 23% YoY from 120, 7% QoQ from 99); mid-market 65 days, Enterprise 145 days. Conversion rates 18.2% (up from 14.5% YoY), ARR/sales $1.7M. Improved via AI scoring, Gong adherence, Outreach/Clari, freemium (1.3 viral).
aspect_summary.Expansion revenue: $42M expansion ARR (52.5% of net new, up 42% YoY to $28.7M in some metrics, 12% QoQ). Upsells $17.8M (62%, ForgeAI), cross-sells $8.0M (28%), seats $2.9M (10%). NRR 121%; driven by AI features, CSM coverage, 68% ARR from existing customers.
